Setup (char 16381-16891)\\n\\n# Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor availability change\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nAmazon SageMaker Model Monitor is no longer open to new customers.\\nExisting customers can continue to use the service as normal. AWS continues to invest in security and availability improvements for\\nModel Monitor, but we do not plan to introduce new features.\\n\\n## Open-source SageMaker AI monitoring solutions + Amazon QuickSight + Amazon CloudWatch\\n\\nThe combination of the open-source Amazon SageMaker AI monitoring solutions, Amazon QuickSight governance dashboards, and Amazon CloudWatch serves as a\\nreplacement for Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor.\\n\\nThe **open-source Amazon SageMaker AI monitoring solutions**\\n(published in the `aws-samples` GitHub organization) provide a highly scalable and\\ncustomizable foundation for comprehensive data and model quality monitoring. They are built on\\nAWS managed services (Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon Athena, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge,\\nAmazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon QuickSight) combined with open-source ML tooling (SageMaker AI\\nMLflow Apps and Evidently AI). The solutions run entirely within your AWS account and scale\\nfrom low-volume batch workloads to high-throughput real-time endpoints. They cover batch\\ninference, real-time endpoints, LLM evaluation, and GPU resource observability, and you adapt\\nthem to your own datasets, models, and drift thresholds.\\n\\n**Inference monitoring with Amazon QuickSight** adds a\\ngovernance layer above your production inference pipelines for real-time and predictive\\nmonitoring. It continuously tracks prediction and data quality metrics, handles delayed ground\\ntruth, and visualizes drift and model-performance trends in executive dashboards. This\\nsolution combines SageMaker AI MLflow Apps and Evidently AI for statistical drift analysis\\nwith an Athena Iceberg data lake, EventBridge-triggered Lambda for scheduled analysis, SNS\\nalerting, and QuickSight dashboards.\\n\\n**Amazon CloudWatch** provides system-level and\\ninference-level monitoring with enhanced metrics for SageMaker endpoints, including invocation\\nlatency, model errors, CPU/GPU utilization, and custom metrics with anomaly detection\\nalarms.\\n\\n## Replacing Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor with open-source solutions, QuickSight, and CloudWatch\\n\\nThis section guides you through replacing your existing Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor\\ndeployment using the open-source Amazon SageMaker AI monitoring solutions (SageMaker AI MLflow\\nApps + Evidently AI), Amazon QuickSight governance dashboards, and Amazon CloudWatch. This\\nsolution supports equivalent and expanded functionality for data quality monitoring, model\\nquality monitoring, bias drift detection, feature attribution drift detection, and system\\nperformance monitoring for models deployed on Amazon SageMaker AI.\\n\\n### Removing Model Monitor\\n\\n#### Discontinue Model Monitor for new monitoring schedules\\n\\nIf your workflow includes creating monitoring schedules using the\\n`DefaultModelMonitor`, `ModelQualityMonitor`,\\n`ModelBiasMonitor`, or `ModelExplainabilityMonitor` classes from the\\nSageMaker Python SDK, or the `CreateMonitoringSchedule` API, transition to the\\nalternatives described in the Configuring Replacements section below.\\n\\n#### Delete existing monitoring schedules\\n\\nMonitoring schedules spin up Processing Job instances (example:\\n`ml.m5.xlarge`) on a recurring schedule. Deleting them helps eliminate ongoing\\ncompute costs.\\n\\n**Using the SageMaker Python SDK:**\\n\\n```\\nimport sagemaker\\nfrom sagemaker.model_monitor import DefaultModelMonitor\\n\\nsession = sagemaker.Session()\\n# List all monitoring schedules\\nschedules = session.sagemaker_client.list_monitoring_schedules()\\n# Delete each schedule\\nfor schedule in schedules['MonitoringScheduleSummaries']:\\n    schedule_name = schedule['MonitoringScheduleName']\\n    print(f\\\"Deleting monitoring schedule: {schedule_name}\\\")\\n    session.sagemaker_client.delete_monitoring_schedule(\\n        MonitoringScheduleName=schedule_name\\n    )\\n```\\n\\n**Using the AWS CLI:**\\n\\n```\\n# List all monitoring schedules\\naws sagemaker list-monitoring-schedules\\n# Delete a specific monitoring schedule\\naws sagemaker delete-monitoring-schedule \\\\\\n    --monitoring-schedule-name \\\"my-data-quality-monitor\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nDeleting a monitoring schedule also stops the schedule if it has not already been\\nstopped. This does not delete the job execution history of the monitoring schedule.\\n\\n### Configuring replacements\\n\\n#### Choosing a monitoring solution\\n\\nThe open-source Amazon SageMaker AI monitoring solutions repository provides seven\\nproduction-ready monitoring solutions built on SageMaker AI MLflow Apps and Evidently AI.\\nSelect the one that matches your inference pattern and operational needs. All of them are\\nopen-source, run inside your AWS account, and are designed to be customized for your\\ndatasets, models, and drift thresholds.\\n\\n| Solution | Inference type | Deployment | Monitoring focus | Best for |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| Predictive ML Batch Monitoring Pipeline | Batch Transform | 2 notebooks (experiment + SageMaker Pipeline) | Data + model quality drift | Periodic batch predictions |\\n| Predictive ML Endpoint Monitoring | Real-time endpoint (Data Capture) | Notebook + CDK Lambda | Data + model quality drift | Real-time endpoints scaled with CDK |\\n| Real-Time Inference Monitoring with Evidently AI + SNS | Real-time endpoint (Data Capture) | Workshop notebook (referral) | Data + model quality drift | Lightweight email alerting on an existing endpoint |\\n| Real-Time Inference Monitoring with QuickSight Dashboards | Real-time endpoint | Notebooks + scripts (Athena Iceberg lake) | Drift + performance + delayed ground truth | Production governance dashboards (see meta-monitoring below) |\\n| LLM Inference Monitoring | Real-time endpoint (Data Capture) | CDK (Step Functions + Lambda) | Generative AI evaluations (safety, relevance, fluency, etc.) | LLM safety and quality monitoring |\\n| SageMaker Resource Observability with Grafana | Real-time endpoint | Single notebook (Amazon Managed Grafana) | GPU/CPU/memory + cost | Multi-model cost and capacity optimization |\\n| LLM Quality Observability with Grafana | Real-time endpoint | Notebook (Managed Grafana + CloudWatch) | Safety, relevance, tone, composite quality | LLM output quality regression detection |\\n\\n#### Getting started with the monitoring solutions\\n\\nThe recommended starting points for replacing Model Monitor's data and model quality\\nmonitoring are the **Predictive ML Batch Monitoring Pipeline**\\n(for batch/Batch Transform workloads) and the **Predictive ML Endpoint\\nMonitoring** solution (for real-time endpoints). Both use the UCI Bank Marketing\\ndataset out of the box, so you can run them end to end before adapting them to your own\\nmodel.\\n\\n**Predictive ML Batch Monitoring Pipeline** (two\\nnotebooks, run in sequence):\\n\\n1. **Experimentation**\\n   (`predictive_ml_experimentation_data_model_monitoring_evidently.ipynb`):\\n   trains an XGBoost model with MLflow tracking, runs Batch Transform inference, then\\n   runs Evidently `DataDriftPreset`, `ClassificationPreset`, and\\n   `DataSummaryPreset`, logging all metrics and HTML/JSON reports to your\\n   MLflow App.\\n2. **Pipeline automation**\\n   (`batch_monitoring_pipeline.ipynb`): operationalizes the workflow into a\\n   SageMaker Pipeline with a `TransformStep` and Evidently\\n   `ProcessingStep`s, an SNS topic for alerts, and an EventBridge schedule.\\n   In Section 2, set `baseline_s3_uri`, `production_s3_uri`,\\n   `mlflow_app_name`, `mlflow_experiment_name` (match Notebook 1),\\n   `notification_email`, and `schedule_expression` (for example,\\n   `rate(1 day)`). Confirm the SNS email subscription before the first run.\\n   Drift thresholds live in `scripts/monitoring_processor.py` (default: alert\\n   when more than 30% of features drift).\\n\\n**Predictive ML Endpoint Monitoring** (notebook, then\\noptional CDK for scale): Open\\n`ml_experimentation_with_data_model_monitoring_evidently_realtime.ipynb`, set\\n`mlflow_app_name` in Section 2, and run Sections 1-8. This trains the model,\\ndeploys a real-time endpoint with Data Capture, and runs Evidently\\n`DataDriftPreset` against the baseline and `ClassificationPreset`\\nagainst ground truth.\\n\\nTo scale, deploy the two Docker-based Lambda functions (data drift and model quality)\\nwith CDK. From `cdk/`, run `npm install`, export the variables\\nprinted in Section 9 (`ENDPOINT_NAME`, `BUCKET`,\\n`PREFIX`, `BASELINE_KEY`, `CAPTURE_PREFIX`,\\n`GROUND_TRUTH_KEY`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`,\\n`MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT`, `FEATURE_COLUMNS`, optional\\n`SNS_TOPIC_ARN`), then run `bash scripts/deploy.sh` (runs\\n`cdk bootstrap` automatically).\\n\\nEnable S3 EventBridge notifications on the bucket and add S3 triggers: data drift on\\n`s3:ObjectCreated:*` under `${PREFIX}/data-capture/`, model quality\\nunder `${PREFIX}/data/ground_truth/`.\\n\\n```\\naws s3api put-bucket-notification-configuration \\\\\\n  --bucket <your-sagemaker-bucket> \\\\\\n  --notification-configuration '{\\\"EventBridgeConfiguration\\\": {}}'\\n```\\n\\nThe model quality Lambda alerts via SNS when a metric falls below its threshold\\n(defaults: F1 0.70, Accuracy 0.80, ROC AUC 0.75; override with\\n`THRESHOLD_F1`, `THRESHOLD_ACCURACY`,\\n`THRESHOLD_ROC_AUC`).\\n\\nThe model quality Lambda alerts via SNS when a metric falls below its threshold\\n(defaults: F1 0.70, Accuracy 0.80, ROC AUC 0.75; override with\\n`THRESHOLD_F1`, `THRESHOLD_ACCURACY`,\\n`THRESHOLD_ROC_AUC`).\\n\\nFor a lightweight alternative on an existing endpoint, the **Real-Time Inference Monitoring with Evidently AI + SNS** solution adds a\\nsingle `FrameworkProcessor` Processing step (`EvidentlyMonitoring`)\\nplus an EventBridge Scheduler and SNS topic, with no data lake or dashboard. It is a\\nreferral to Section 8 of Notebook 06 in the amazon-sagemaker-from-idea-to-production workshop.
